Ireland football team faces boycott calls over Israel matches

Calls for the Republic of Ireland's national football team to boycott upcoming fixtures against Israel have intensified. The Irish FA is reportedly facing pressure from athletes' groups and individuals concerned about the ongoing conflict. The matches are scheduled for September 27 in Hungary and October 4 in Serbia, with neutral venues and no away fans reportedly being considered due to the contentious nature of the fixtures. The controversy escalated when the Israel FA issued a statement criticizing Republic of Ireland coach Stephen Kenny, accusing him of "stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy" following comments he made.
